summary: Discovery call with Solstice Diagnostics to understand requirements for an on-prem, air-gapped Redwood Private deployment. Main concerns: offline update process, approved hardware list (GPUs + network), strict logging and key management, FedRAMP/HIPAA adjacency, and pilot acceptance criteria. AE + SE will follow up with diagrams, a sizing spreadsheet, and SOC/crypto docs; customer to confirm hardware and internal timelines.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-15 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~60m | Recorded by Fireflies
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Marisol (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Park (CTO, Solstice), Marcus Hale (Head of Infra), Priya Sinha (Compliance Lead)
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, from Redwood, this is Jordan, I'm the account lead, and with me is Marisol from our solutions engineering team. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Elena: Hi Jordan, doing well, thanks. Marcus is here and Priya as well. Appreciate you taking the time.
[00:12] Marcus: Morning all, quick heads up we're on a slightly constrained network today so audio might glitch, bear with us.
[00:18] Jordan: No problem. The agenda I proposed was a quick run through your isolation needs, hardware constraints, update cadence, and then map to deployment options — hosted, dedicated, private — and where an air-gapped on-prem fit. Is that still good?
[00:29] Priya: Yes, that's perfect. We really need to validate the offline update flow and the auditability of every change.
[00:34] Marisol: Great. Real quick, can you confirm the regulatory targets, Priya? I know you mentioned HIPAA in the doc, any federal or FedRAMP adjacency?
[00:42] Priya: Primary is HIPAA and state-level PHI controls; long-term we may require FedRAMP consulting for some joint programs, but initial pilot is strictly HIPAA + internal audit trails.
[00:53] Jordan: Got it. Marcus, can you describe the datacenter environment? racks, switches, any airgap specifics?
[00:59] Marcus: Sure. We're collocated in a private cage, no outbound internet on the management plane. We have jump servers for updates that are physically isolated. For compute nodes, we have a mix: 2x A100 40GB (older), 4x A100 80GB pending procurement, and a couple of Ampere-like infer chips for smaller models. Our network topology is spine-leaf, but the NVLink fabric is limited to pairs; we don't have full NVSwitch.
[01:25] Marisol: Okay that's helpful — limited NVLink/full NVSwitch affects some large-model throughput patterns. For our runtime, we can support mixed GPU SKUs but certain optimizations assume NVSwitch-like connectivity for partitioned attention. We'll capture that in the sizing spreadsheet.
[01:39] Elena: Clarify "updates" — we cannot allow automatic outbound connections. All updates must be brought in via a physical media process and validated against signatures.
[01:47] Jordan: Understood. Redwood Private supports offline update packages. The typical flow we propose is: Redwood generates a signed bundle (tar/gz) with artifacts and a signed manifest; you ingest via your jumpbox, we provide verification tooling that can run locally against your HSM/KMS. Does that line up with your security expectations?
[02:05] Priya: Yes, but we need HSM integration. Keys must be under our control. Who holds the signing keys initially?
[02:12] Marisol: The typical pattern is Redwood signs build artifacts with our build CI key, but for air-gapped customers we provide a mechanism to re-sign or rotate signatures using your HSM before activation. We can also support delivering unsigned artifacts and a reference manifest so you can sign locally — it's a bit more manual but fully air-gapped.
[02:30] Marcus: That sounds okay. We'll need documentation on the exact verification commands and expected exit codes. Also, does Redwood support an offline attestation step? e.g., a checksum + signature verification tool?
[02:40] Marisol: Yes, we have a small verification utility (sha256 + RSA/ECDSA verify) that runs on Python 3.8+; we can provide a static binary if you prefer no python. It returns non-zero on mismatch.
[02:49] Elena: Good. What about telemetry? Right now we cannot push any usage metrics offsite.
[02:54] Jordan: For Private air-gapped installs we have two modes: telemetry disabled (no outbound) or telemetry buffered to a local observability stack. If you choose disabled, you'll get no usage reporting to Redwood; your console will be a private instance. If you want aggregated metrics later we can do batched export via signed bundles.
[03:12] Priya: We likely want telemetry disabled for the pilot.
[03:15] Jordan: Noted. Marcus, about storage — where will model weights live? On an internal object store?
[03:20] Marcus: Yes, on an S3-compatible object store behind the private network. Access controlled via internal IAM.
[03:25] Marisol: That's fine; our runtime can read from S3-compatible endpoints. We'll need endpoint, auth method (HMAC or STS), and network ACL requirements.
[03:33] Marcus: We use HMAC keys rotated every 30 days.
[03:36] Marisol: We'll add that to the integration checklist.
[03:39] Jordan: Quick question on scale: what's your expected QPS and concurrent sessions for the pilot?
[03:44] Elena: Initially low — 5–10 concurrent inference sessions, spiking to maybe 50 during testing. Latency target is <300ms for the 512 token typical path.
[03:54] Marisol: With your GPUs — 2x A100 40GB + 4x 80GB planned — we can likely meet that for mid-sized models, but for larger 13B+ models we may need model sharding and will see latency impacts without NVSwitch. We'll propose quantization options as well.
[04:12] Marcus: Is there any support for running with GPUs at different mem sizes? like mixing 40GB and 80GB?
[04:17] Marisol: Yes, but performance is asymmetric. We treat them as separate pools and will route requests accordingly. For large models spanning GPUs, we prefer homogeneous clusters.
[04:25] Elena: The legal team also asked about audit logs. We need immutable logs for every inference request tied back to a request id, user id, and service account. Retention policy must be configurable to 7 years.
[04:38] Priya: Also exportable in a format that our SIEM ingests — JSONL preferred.
[04:44] Jordan: Our Private deployment provides local audit logs with configurable retention. For very long retention like 7 years, we'd recommend archiving to your internal cold storage. We can ship logs as JSONL and include schema.
[04:56] Marcus: About authentication — SSO/SAML and service-to-service RBAC. We need SCIM + SAML for user provisioning and token rotation for internal services.
[05:05] Marisol: Supported. We expose a local auth proxy that integrates with your SAML IdP and supports SCIM for provisioning; service tokens are short lived and rotate with your KMS if you want HSM-backed signing.
[05:16] Elena: Do you support customer-managed KMS with HSM? We cannot have keys in Redwood cloud for this deployment.
[05:22] Jordan: Yes, we can integrate with customer KMS/HSM. For the pilot, customers typically deploy an HSM appliance or use on-prem KMS, and we integrate via PKCS#11 or KMIP.
[05:33] Marcus: Any constraints on HSM types? We currently have a Thales Luna 8 and a Vault HSM module.
[05:40] Marisol: We have integrations with both Thales and HashiCorp Vault HSM plugins. PKCS#11 support is available; we will share recommended API calls in the checklist.
[05:49] Priya: On legal controls: can you guarantee zero data exfiltration? Our lawyers will want contractual language.
[05:55] Jordan: We provide contractual options in our enterprise agreement for Private on-prem installs, including data residency and no-remote-access clauses. We'll share a redline-friendly doc.
[06:05] Elena: Network-wise, our ops team will want to know what ports need to be opened for internal routing, and any temporary ports for initial install media validation.
[06:13] Marisol: We'll provide a detailed network diagram: required ports between controller nodes, runtime, and storage. For air-gapped, the initial signature verification only needs outbound to nothing — it's all offline. But if you choose to run periodic batched telemetry exports later, we'll provide SSH/SCP patterns or signed bundle transfer steps.
[06:31] Marcus: Do you have a footprint estimate for a minimal cluster? CPU, RAM, disk?
[06:36] Marisol: Yes — minimal cluster (for pilot): 3 controller nodes (4 vCPU, 16GB RAM each), one orchestration node, and GPU nodes as you have. Diskwise, model weights — depending on model — plan 500GB per 7B model and 2TB per 70B; we'll provide a per-model disk estimate in the sizing doc.
[06:53] Elena: For acceptance criteria, compliance will require a runbook for update/rollback, a successful crypto verification, and a recorded test of a simulated incident.
[07:02] Priya: We want a test where you produce a signed bundle and we intentionally tamper with the manifest and show that verification fails. Also, a failover test across two racks.
[07:11] Jordan: Totally doable. We'll include step-by-step tests.
[07:14] Marisol: One operational note — on model provisioning: for very large models we recommend quantized variants to reduce memory and inference time, we can assist with a quantization profile based on your latency targets.
[07:26] Marcus: Any licensing for model weights? if you pull an open model vs. proprietary — how does that change the update flow?
[07:32] Jordan: Licensing doesn't change the airgap mechanics, but for commercial models we need to ensure EULAs allow on-prem installations. We'll capture license fields in the manifest.
[07:41] Elena: Potential blockers: procurement timeline — we may not have the 80GB cards until May. Pilot ideally in April but procurement could push to June.
[07:49] Jordan: Noted. We can run an initial pilot on smaller models and hybrid CPU inference while you wait for GPUs.
[07:54] Priya: Encryption at rest — we need to know if Redwood encrypts model files by default or relies on your storage encryption.
[07:59] Marisol: We support both. If you want host-level encryption with customer KMS keys, we can do envelope encryption with your KMS. We'll document the key flow.
[08:09] Marcus: How do we handle emergency patches? Our policy requires a sealed change process and attestations.
[08:15] Jordan: Emergency patches will be distributed as signed bundles with an incident tag; we'll include a separate audit trail and a migration plan. We'll also support an approval workflow where a signed attestation from your compliance owner is required before apply.
[08:29] Elena: Can Redwood run in a fully disconnected mode, no control plane connectivity to Redwood?
[08:33] Marisol: Yes, Private can be deployed with the control plane local to your VPC/airgapped environment. You get the console on-prem. There's also a hybrid option where the control plane is customer-managed but Redwood still hosts some non-sensitive services — but for you, fully local sounds like the requirement.
[08:49] Jordan: Any specific logging format for your SIEM ingestion?
[08:52] Priya: JSONL, timestamp ISO8601, and an md5 or sha field on payloads. Also we need a mapping doc to our SIEM fields.
[08:59] Marisol: We'll include a sample JSONL and a mapping file.
[09:03] Marcus: A question about support SLAs — for on-prem, what is the TTR for critical incidents?
[09:09] Jordan: We offer enterprise SLAs with a 1-hour acknowledged response and 4-hour mitigation window for critical incidents for Dedicated and Private customers on an enterprise plan. We'll include options in the contract.
[09:20] Elena: Can you provide references of other regulated healthcare customers who've done this?
[09:25] Jordan: Yes, we can share redacted case studies and reference contacts under NDA. We'll include a short list.
[09:31] Priya: Ok good. For the signing of artifacts: can you integrate with our internal CA for certs?
[09:36] Marisol: Yes, we can accept your CA-signed certs for internal TLS endpoints. We will document the CSR/CSR signing cadence.
[09:44] Jordan: Alright, timecheck — we're at about 35 minutes in. If it's ok, we'll move to actions and next steps and then close.
[09:50] Elena: Sounds good.
[09:51] Jordan: Recap: We'll send an air-gapped deployment checklist, network diagram, verification binary, and sizing spreadsheet. You'll validate hardware SKUs and procurement timing. We'll schedule an on-site pre-audit call with Priya and Marcus. Any other asks?
[10:04] Marcus: Please also include writeup for mixed GPU behavior and any recommended schedulers or routing policies.
[10:10] Marisol: Will do. We'll also suggest batching/quantization configs to hit your latency target.
[10:15] Priya: And legal will want the no-exfiltration clause example.
[10:18] Jordan: We'll attach a sample contract clause. Final Qs?
[10:21] Elena: None from me. Thanks, this was helpful.
[10:24] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up by Thursday with the artifacts. Appreciate the time.
[10:28] End of recording.
notes: Customer requires offline signed bundles and HSM integration
Telemetry to be disabled for pilot
Hardware procurement may delay pilot start
